brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full bases stacked at (1,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2 (piece:1,0,0/1,0,1/1,0,2;full), held together by snap:1,0,0 and snap:1,0,1.

Two half bases on level 0 are joint-bolted to the core: piece:2,-1,0;half-s with drawer:0#2,-1#cut, bolted by jointBolt:0#1,0#1, and piece:0,1,0;half-n with drawer:0#0,1#cut, bolted by jointBolt:0#0,1#1. Drawers only fit on half bases, and the configurator offers no place to stack anything on a half base. So the drawers sit beside the column, not under it.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:1,0,2~hex-bin-full-div3, an open three-section bin on the level-2 base, with no cover added.

finish.summary: Three-storey tower: one column of full bases, an open three-section bin on top, and two drawers in joint-bolted half bases on the ground floor. check_build found no errors and meshClash came back clear. 19 open faces could still take decorative caps; that is info only. No load ratings are claimed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
